Suppose B is a subgroup of the symmetric group S
                                                             Ω on an infinite set Ω.
Will the amalgamated free product SΩ ∗B SΩ of two copies of SΩ with amalgamation
of B be embeddable in SΩ ? This is a weakened form of the group case of Question 4.4
in (G. M. Bergman, Indag. Math., 18 (2007), 349–403).
    It is known that SΩ ∗B SΩ need not be so embeddable by a map respecting B
(Algebra Number Theory, 3 (2009), 847–879, § 10).                    G. M. Bergman
  ∗ No, not necessarily: take Ω countably infinite, B a subgroup of S which is
                                                                            Ω
not Borel, and ϕ : SΩ ∗B SΩ → SΩ an injective group homomorphism. Let ϕ1
be the restriction of ϕ to the first copy of SΩ and ϕ2 that to the second. Each
ϕi is continuous (A. S. Kechris, C. Rosendal, Proc. Lond. Math. Soc., 94, no. 2
(2007), 302–350), so im(ϕi ) is Borel in SΩ (as a continuous injective image of a Polish
space). Now B = ϕ−1                    −1
                      1 (ϕ(B)) = ϕ1 (im(ϕ1 ) ∩ im(ϕ2 )) is Borel, a contradiction.
(S. M. Corson, Letter of 26 January 2026; see also https://kourovkanotebookorg.
wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/solution-of-21.15.pdf.)
